# Resolve enterprise admin-configuration direction conflict

## Description

This investigation resolves the conflicting enterprise feedback on administrative
simplicity: one strategic account wants fewer configuration options exposed
("too many knobs"), while another explicitly wants more fine-grained controls
per project. It consolidates the unconsolidated feedback, establishes which
direction (or reconciliation of both) takes precedence, and produces a decision
that the admin-configuration implementation work builds against.

## Scope

- Consolidate the enterprise account feedback about administrative
  configuration from all channels through which it arrived, resolving the
  partial contradictions documented in the strategy.
- Determine whose feedback takes precedence and on what basis (account tier,
  product strategy alignment, feasibility), or whether both can be satisfied
  through a tiered design (e.g. simple defaults with advanced per-project
  controls available on demand).
- Identify the specific configuration surfaces in the RHOAI console that each
  direction concerns (against Dashboard and OdhDashboardConfig capabilities
  described in architecture context).
- Produce a written decision record: the chosen direction, the affected
  configuration surfaces, and recommended scope for the implementation work.
- Flag any identified friction points that fall outside the Dashboard component
  for handoff.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All known enterprise feedback on administrative configuration is collected
  into one place, with sources and contradictions made explicit.
- A decision is recorded on which direction takes precedence, or a concrete
  reconciliation that satisfies both accounts, with rationale.
- The decision enumerates the configuration surfaces it applies to.
- The decision is confirmed with the strategy owner / product stakeholders
  before implementation begins.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 — Administration should be simpler (accounts request conflicting
  directions: fewer exposed options vs. more fine-grained per-project controls).

# Define data-scientist onboarding scope and time baseline

## Description

This investigation defines what "onboarding a new data scientist" covers and
establishes where the time is currently spent, so that the "less than a day"
target becomes measurable and the right onboarding improvements get built. It
is a cross-component journey spanning the console (Dashboard) and the workbench
layer (Notebooks).

## Scope

- Decide the onboarding boundary: which of cluster access, project setup, first
  workbench, and first deployed model (the strategy's open question) count as
  "onboarding a new data scientist".
- Map the current onboarding journey end to end and measure (or estimate from
  representative trials) where elapsed time and friction occur today.
- Identify which friction points fall in the console and which in the workbench
  / notebook-server layer, so the follow-up work can be assigned to the right
  teams.
- Define a measurable success metric for the "less than a day" target under the
  chosen boundary (e.g. time-to-first-successful-workbench, time-to-first-model
  for a representative new user persona).
- Verify the chosen boundary against the downstream epic structure: the
  follow-up implementation work covers a console layer (Dashboard) and a
  workbench layer (Notebooks) — the strategy's Affected Components. If the
  boundary includes a stage whose friction is not absorbed by either layer
  (notably "first deployed model", whose friction would fall to model-serving
  surfaces outside the two affected components), the scope decision must say
  so explicitly and route that friction to a separate follow-up strategy
  rather than leaving it unowned.
- Produce a written scope decision and prioritized friction list.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The onboarding boundary is decided and recorded, covering the strategy's open
  question (cluster access, project setup, first workbench, first deployed
  model).
- A baseline of where onboarding time is spent today exists, with method and
  limitations noted.
- The success metric for "less than a day" is operationalized and measurable.
- Friction items are split by owning area (console vs. workbench layer).
- If the chosen boundary includes stages outside the console/workbench layers
  (e.g. first deployed model on serving surfaces), those friction items are
  explicitly routed to a separate follow-up strategy, with none left unowned.
- The scope decision is confirmed with the strategy owner before implementation
  begins.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 — Onboarding a new data scientist should take "less than a day"
  (currently undefined what onboarding includes or where the day is spent).

# Identify target enterprise tools and integration scope

## Description

This investigation identifies which enterprise tools the consolidated feedback
refers to and what "integrate better" concretely means for each, producing a
bounded, prioritized integration recommendation. The strategy names no specific
tools, so no integration work can be scoped until this resolves.

## Scope

- Consolidate the enterprise account feedback to extract the specific tools and
  tool categories behind "integrate better with existing enterprise tooling".
- For each candidate tool, determine the integration form that would deliver
  the value (e.g. authentication/SSO, identity/group sync, source control,
  CI/CD, monitoring/observability, data governance) at a capability level —
  without committing to specific API designs.
- Identify which RHOAI component each integration would touch (Dashboard,
  Notebooks, or another component) so the implementation work lands with the
  right team. Where an assignment differs from the component initially
  assigned to the integration implementation work (a placeholder pending this
  investigation's outcome), the recommendation must flag the reassignment
  explicitly so the affected epic is moved to the correct owning team rather
  than left on the placeholder.
- Assess feasibility and rough effort per candidate integration.
- Produce a bounded, prioritized recommendation of which integrations to pursue
  this release, with the affected components and an explicit not-pursuing list
  (the strategy has no out-of-scope boundary — this provides one).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A consolidated list of the enterprise tools the feedback actually refers to
  exists, with sources.
- Each candidate integration has a described integration form, affected RHOAI
  component, and feasibility assessment.
- A prioritized, bounded recommendation identifies what is pursued this release
  and what is explicitly deferred.
- Any component/team reassignment of the integration implementation work away
  from its initial placeholder assignment is stated explicitly in the
  recommendation.
- The recommendation is confirmed with the strategy owner before implementation
  begins.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 — The platform should "integrate better" with existing enterprise
  tooling (no specific tools named in the consolidated feedback).

# Enterprise admin configuration experience

## Description

This epic delivers the administrative configuration experience chosen by the
preceding investigation into the conflicting enterprise feedback: either the
simplified configuration surface, the fine-grained per-project controls, or a
reconciliation of both. The Dashboard is the console surface for per-component
feature flags and defaults (via the OdhDashboardConfig CR) and is where
administrators interact with configuration today.

## Scope

- Implement the configuration-experience direction recorded in the
  investigation's decision (simplification, granularity, or tiered
  combination), across the configuration surfaces the decision enumerates.
- Cover the relevant console surfaces for administering configuration
  defaults and per-project overrides.
- Include incidental documentation touch-ups (updated captions, labels, or
  references in existing admin docs) that fall out of the same change — no new
  doc topics are authored here.
- Validate the experience against representative administrator personas from
  the consolidated enterprise feedback.

Exact scope is finalized from the investigation's decision record; do not
pre-commit to specific settings or UI structures beyond what it specifies.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The configuration experience matches the direction and surfaces enumerated in
  the investigation's confirmed decision.
- An administrator from the "too many knobs" account persona can complete
  representative configuration tasks with fewer exposed options (or the
  equivalent chosen direction), verified by the success measure the decision
  defines.
- An administrator from the fine-grained-controls persona retains the control
  the decision requires (or the reconciliation satisfies both), verified
  likewise.
- The change does not remove capability required by existing users that the
  decision did not authorize removing.
- Incidental doc touch-ups from the same change are included.
- Because this work may replace existing admin configuration behavior: a
  rollback path or feature flag allows reverting to the current experience.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 — Administration should be simpler (conflicting directions: fewer
  exposed options vs. more fine-grained per-project controls).

# Enterprise tooling integration

## Description

This epic delivers the enterprise tooling integrations selected by the
preceding tool-identification investigation, at the scope that investigation
bounds. It implements the prioritized integration forms (e.g. authentication,
identity sync, source control, CI/CD, monitoring) for the identified tools, on
the RHOAI components the investigation assigns them to.

## Scope

- Implement the prioritized integrations from the investigation's
  recommendation, in the forms it describes (capability level; specific
  protocols and API designs are implementation decisions for the team).
- Adjust the Dashboard surfaces needed for any user-facing integration the
  recommendation includes.
- Cover handoff of any integration the investigation assigns to a different
  component's team — that work is tracked there, not here.
- Include incidental documentation touch-ups that fall out of the same change —
  no new doc topics are authored here.

Exact scope, target tools, and affected components are finalized from the
investigation's confirmed recommendation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each integration the recommendation prioritizes for this release is
  delivered at the described form and verified against the identified
  enterprise tool.
- Integrations the recommendation defers are explicitly not attempted.
- Representative enterprise users (per the consolidated feedback) confirm the
  described integration value is delivered.
- Incidental doc touch-ups from the same change are included.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 — The platform should "integrate better" with existing enterprise
  tooling (specific tools and integration scope defined by the preceding
  investigation).
